cvEn:
Yosef Taxon, son of Lea and Yaakov, was born on 14 Kislev 5686 (1 December 1925) in Jerusalem. He expanded the basic education he received at school through constant self-study. He was especially interested in literature, the land of Israel and general history. He specialized in dyeing fine leathers, and he supported his parents with his earnings.

From the first days of the events, he was among the defenders of the Old City, until the liberators broke through Zion Gate. Even then, as before, he refused the offer to rest a little behind the front, saying that he would not leave the place he had grown attached to as long as the fighting continued. During a fierce Arab assault on the Batei Mahseh area of the Old City, he was hit by a bullet and fell on 14 Iyar 5708 (23 May 1948). In August 1967 he was brought to his final rest in a mass grave on the Mount of Olives. His name is engraved on the memorial erected in the Military Cemetery on Mount Herzl in memory of the fallen of the Jewish Quarter and of the fighters who fell in the battle for Jerusalem and were buried on the Mount of Olives.
